summary: Plan community-led agricultural interventions and track results with practical rural assessment, climate-risk and monitoring exercises. Explore the course.
lede: Sustainable agriculture and rural development links community priorities with suitable farming options and project monitoring. For intermediate rural and agricultural development practitioners, the course develops skills in participatory needs and livelihood assessments, climate-risk review, community planning, and indicator tracking. You practise turning field evidence into work plans and budgets, coordinating partners, and reviewing intervention results with communities.
audienceIntro: This intermediate course suits practitioners who assess rural conditions, coordinate agricultural interventions and report on results with community and institutional partners.
prerequisites: Intermediate-level familiarity with agricultural or rural development activities is recommended. No programming is required; exercises use planning and reporting artefacts, including spreadsheet-based tracking.
